question: Which of the following is NOT a quantitative method of credit control?
solution:
The correct answer is** "Moral suasion".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Moral suasion** is defined as the attempt to coerce private economic activity through governmental exhortation in directions not defined by law.
 
• It is used in reference to **central banks**.
 
• This is used by central banks to influence the market and public emotions that they are in control of the economy.
 
• It is a **qualitative** tool.
 
• It is a request by RBI to commercial banks to take specific steps according to the economy's trends.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Credit control **is the strategy used by businesses to increase the sales of products by extension of credit to potential customers or clients.
 
• Credit control is used by the Reserve Bank of India.
 
• There are** two types** of methods:
 
• Quantitative methods:
 
 
• Open market operations
 
• Cash reserve ratio
 
• Statutory liquidity ratio
 
 
 
• Qualitative methods: 
 
 
• Margin requirements
 
• Consumer credit regulation
 
• RBI guidelines 
 
• Rationing of credit
 
• Direct action
